grammar_focus: 介词 + 关系代词(the repayment of which…)、whether … or … 引导的从句、同位语从句 that(a rule/the fact that…)、情态动词 + have done 对过去的推测(may/must/can't have been)、tell/instruct sb to do + 过去分词作定语(checks drawn by himself)(NCE4 无 KS 页,考点由课文结构自取;IP:源为消费者法著作,内容为通用银行法概念(事实性、不可版权),已用 100% 原创行文复述,无人物;题材=银行与客户的法律关系·无害;美语化 check/favor;第四册第12课·第二册收官课)
scene: 当一个人在银行开立活期账户,多数人以为自己不过是把钱交去保管。法律上的真相却更古怪:客户其实是在把钱借给银行,于是银行成了债务人——这笔债的偿还,他可以随时要求,或取现金,或开一张支票付给别人。因此,银行与客户之间最根本的关系,是债务人与债权人的关系;至于谁是哪一方,取决于账户是有余额还是透支。不过,除了这个简单的概念,双方还彼此负有一整套义务,其中许多会招来麻烦与纠葛。然而,银行客户不同于——比方说——普通的买货人,他很少能抱怨法律对自己不公。银行必须听从它客户的指示,而不听任何别人的。当一个人头一回开户,他会吩咐银行只为他本人开出的支票扣款,并留下几份签名样本,好让职员比对。有一条极硬的规矩:凡是签名被伪造的支票,银行无权动用客户的钱去兑付。哪怕那伪造也许曾极其高明,也毫无分别:银行仍被要求认得自己客户的笔迹。正因如此,银行如今普遍采用的、把客户姓名印在其支票上的做法,对客户其实并无风险。即便这一习惯当真便利了某次伪造,承担损失的也是银行,而非客户。

grammar_card.title: 介词+关系代词 / whether…or / 同位语从句 / 情态+have done / tell sb to do
grammar_card.intro: ①介词 + 关系代词:the repayment of which he may demand;the account on which he draws checks。②whether … or …:depends on whether the account is in credit or overdrawn。③同位语从句 that,解释前面抽象名词:a rule that the bank must recognize the signature。④情态词 + have + 过去分词,对过去推测:may have been / must have been / can't have been。⑤tell/instruct sb to do;过去分词作定语:checks drawn by himself。

rows: the repayment of which he may demand
whether it is in credit or overdrawn
a rule that the bank must recognize it
the forgery may have been clever

specialRules.rule: 情态词 + have + 过去分词表示对过去的推测:may have(也许曾)、must have(一定曾)、can't have(不可能曾)。
同位语从句用 that 引导且 that 不作成分(不可省、不能换 which);定语从句里 that 要在从句中充当成分。
specialRules.mark: 同位语 that ≠ 定语 that

specialRules.rule: 美式拼写:check(支票,英式 cheque)、favor(有利,英式 favour)。本课已按美语写。

prelisten.q: Listen and answer — Why is there no risk to the customer when a bank prints the customer's name on his checks?
options: Because the bank, not the customer, must bear any loss from forgery
Because printed names can never be forged
Because the customer pays extra insurance
Because the bank ignores all signatures

passage: When a person opens a current account at a bank, most people imagine they are simply handing their money over for safekeeping. In law the truth is stranger: the customer is actually lending money to the bank, so that the bank becomes a debtor — a debt the repayment of which he may demand at any moment, either in cash or by writing a check in favor of someone else. The basic tie between a bank and its customer is therefore that of debtor and creditor, and who is which depends on whether the account is in credit or is overdrawn. Beyond that simple idea, however, the two owe each other a whole set of obligations, and many of these can lead to problems and complications. Yet a bank customer, unlike, say, an ordinary buyer of goods, can rarely complain that the law is stacked against him. The bank must obey its customer's instructions, and no one else's. When someone first opens an account, he tells the bank to debit it only for checks drawn by himself, and he leaves specimens of his signature so that the staff can compare them. There is a very firm rule that the bank has no right to pay out a customer's money on a check whose signature has been forged. It makes no difference that the forgery may have been an extremely clever one: the bank is still expected to recognize its own customer's hand. For this reason there is really no danger to the customer in the practice, now widely adopted by banks, of printing the customer's name on his checks. Even if that habit should happen to facilitate a forgery, it is the bank, and not the customer, that must bear the loss.

stage5.stem: "It is a debt the repayment ___ which he may demand at any time."(介词+关系代词,‘其偿还’,填介词)
stage5.stem_cn: 这是一笔他可随时要求偿还的债。

stage5.stem: "The account ___ which he draws checks is a current one."(介词+关系代词;开支票所凭的账户,填与 draw 搭配的介词)
stage5.stem_cn: 他开支票所凭的那个账户是活期账户。

stage5.stem: "The rule ___ which the bank acts protects the customer."(介词+关系代词;银行依据的规则,填与 act 搭配的介词)
stage5.stem_cn: 银行依据的那条规则保护着客户。

stage5.stem: "Who is which depends on ___ the account is in credit or overdrawn."(‘是否/…还是…’,填连词)
stage5.stem_cn: 谁是谁,取决于账户是有余额还是透支。

stage5.stem: "The bank must check ___ the signature is genuine or forged."(‘是否…’,填连词)
stage5.stem_cn: 银行必须核查签名是真是假。

stage5.stem: "It matters little ___ the forgery is clumsy or skilful."(‘无论…还是…’,填连词)
stage5.stem_cn: 伪造是拙劣还是高明,都无关紧要。

stage5.stem: "There is a firm rule ___ the bank must recognize its customer's signature."(同位语从句,解释 rule 的内容,填连词)
stage5.stem_cn: 有一条硬规矩:银行必须认得客户的签名。

stage5.stem: "The fact ___ the account is overdrawn changes who owes whom."(同位语从句,解释 fact,填连词)
stage5.stem_cn: 账户透支这一事实,改变了谁欠谁。

stage5.stem: "He accepts the idea ___ he is lending the bank money."(同位语从句,解释 idea,填连词)
stage5.stem_cn: 他接受了这样一个观念:他是在借钱给银行。

stage5.stem: "The forgery may ___ been a very clever one."(may + ___ + 过去分词,对过去的推测,填中间的助动词)
stage5.stem_cn: 那伪造也许曾是非常高明的。

stage5.stem: "The clerk must ___ missed the forged signature."(must + ___ + 过去分词,对过去的肯定推测,填中间的助动词)
stage5.stem_cn: 那职员一定是漏看了伪造的签名。

stage5.stem: "He can't ___ signed it, for he was abroad."(can't + ___ + 过去分词,对过去的否定推测,填中间的助动词)
stage5.stem_cn: 他不可能签过字,因为他当时在国外。

stage5.stem: "He tells the bank ___ his account only for his own checks."(tell sb 后接不定式;‘吩咐银行扣款’,填正确形式)
stage5.stem_cn: 他吩咐银行只为他本人的支票扣款。

stage5.stem: "The bank may pay only checks ___ by the customer himself."(过去分词作定语,‘由…开出的’;draw 的过去分词)
stage5.stem_cn: 银行只能支付客户本人开出的支票。

stage5.stem: "The name ___ on his checks does not put him at risk."(过去分词作定语,‘印在…上的’;print 的过去分词)
stage5.stem_cn: 印在支票上的姓名不会使他有风险。

stage5.stem: "A person or bank that owes money is a ___."(“债务人、借方”用哪个词)
"To copy a signature falsely in order to cheat is to ___ it."(“伪造”用哪个词)
"To take up and start using a practice is to ___ it."(“采用、采纳”用哪个词)
stage5.stem_cn: 接受并开始采用某种做法。
